    3 · Where are the key levels?

    Dealer gamma by strike

    How to read this ▸

    Assumption: dealers are long the calls (bought from producers overwriting) and short the puts (sold to hedgers). CME open interest doesn't show who holds what, so treat this as a model, not a fact.

    Green bars: dealers are long gamma there. To stay hedged they sell rallies and buy dips, which tends to calm price and pin it near big strikes. Red bars: dealers are short gamma. They have to buy rallies and sell dips, so moves tend to get bigger.

    Flip: the futures price where the net changes sign. Above the flip the market is usually calmer, below it usually wilder (or the reverse, depending on the sign). The “If price moves…” view shows that directly.

    Units: futures lots dealers would trade per 10¢ move.

    4 · Who holds the options?

    CFTC options-only positioning

    Delta-equivalent contracts. Derived as combined (futures + options) minus futures-only

    GroupFutures netOptions net Δw/wVol spreads
    How to read this ▸

    Vol spreads are straddles, strangles and verticals. A rising figure means funds are positioning for a bigger move without picking a direction.

    Producer options net Δ shows commercial hedging. When it falls, producers are buying puts or overwriting calls.
